items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: My brother, Jujus, was playing guitar. And my brother was playing bass, Sylvester. And we had a nice trio.

ctx.x: You played chords in mandolin. How did you play that? With a flat pick? Yeah.

Played lead on that. I played in mandolin. My brother, Jujus, was playing guitar. And my brother was playing bass, Sylvester. And we had a nice trio. We used to make a lot of money. We used to go around serenading people at the different hotels in Paris Christiane, Luxie, Gulfport. We used to go all around, I think. And, uh, serenading. Go from house to house. We made nice money. Sometimes we used to come back seven, five, eighty dollars. A night. We used to make nice money, I think. Oh, from drums, I wanted to…

items.title: Crescent City Crystals: Dave Bailey, Harold Christophe, Albert Delone, Sylvester Handy Interview, 1963-11-13
items.q: you worked up late at the La Vida when John had the band there, John and Handy? Oh, yeah.

ctx.x: Born in New Orleans and the Trimmy.

Trimmy? Oh, I know. From Trimmy to the Rocky Green. Like London Avenue. 7-Watt, you know? What... Who taught you to play guitar? Now, who taught me how to play guitar? My father played guitar, you see? Yeah. But my first instrument, I used to pick up his guitar. Uh-huh. And all that harmony was right in my head. Yeah. Sure, I guess from listening to him, you pick up... Yeah, and definitely I would get beaten for fooling the guitar. Yeah. You know what I mean? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. But then I started out on the…

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: I believe it was Sylvester who told me you had a band where you were playing mandolin. Yeah. And him playing bass violin.

ctx.x: No. Let me just ask you something. I believe it must have been before you got put the horn. I believe it was Sylvester who told me you had a band where you were playing mandolin. Yeah. And him playing bass violin. When was that? It was after you played drums?

Well, I was playing drums then, but the night I was off, the freels would go up here on the front street and go from house to house and walk up on the porch. They started playing and people would come out. They had a big hotel up here, right here in the corner at that time. Took up the whole block, the whole square.
